subject: Energy
title: Tidal Energy
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tidal Energy usable.

hook.text: Tides are driven by the Moon's gravity—their rhythm is perfectly predictable, unlike wind or sunshine.

buildup.text: Tidal barrages work like dams across estuaries—water flows through turbines as tides rise and fall.

discovery.text: France's La Rance barrage has produced power since 1966—240 MW from tidal flows in the English Channel.

twist.text: Tidal stream turbines are like underwater wind turbines—they sit on the seabed and spin in tidal currents.

climax.text: Tidal energy is reliable but limited geographically—only coasts with large tidal ranges are economically viable.

punchline.text: The Moon pulls the ocean—and turbines catch the flow.

quiz.question: What makes tidal energy uniquely predictable?
